lessons.title: How a sign is built
lessons.summary: The five building blocks every sign uses, and how to read the cards.

blocks.text: Every sign is made from a few [[parameters]]. If you learn to notice them, new signs get much easier to remember.

items: [[Palm orientation|palm-orientation]]: which way your palm faces.
[[Location|location]]: where the sign happens, like the forehead or in front of the chest.
[[Non-manual markers|non-manual-marker]]: what your face, head and body do.

blocks.text: Each card shows the signer from the front, so their right hand appears on your left. The signer uses the right hand as the [[dominant hand|dominant-hand]].

items: A faded copy of the hand shows where a movement starts.
The solid hand shows where it ends.
Red arrows show the path between them.

blocks.text: In HELLO above, the faded hand starts near the forehead and the arrow shows it moving outward.

lessons.title: The manual alphabet
lessons.summary: Letters for fingerspelling names and words that don't have a sign.

blocks.text: [[Fingerspelling|fingerspelling]] uses one [[handshape]] per letter. Hold your dominant hand near your shoulder with the palm facing out, and keep it steady while your fingers change shape.
Most letters hold still. J and Z are the two that move: J is drawn in the air with the pinky, and Z is drawn with the index finger.

items: Don't bounce your hand for each letter. Let the shapes flow into each other.
Say the word, not the letters. Practice reading whole words by shape.
For a double letter, slide the hand slightly sideways instead of making the shape twice.

lessons.title: How ASL sentences are ordered
lessons.summary: Time first, topic next, and what happens to English words like "the" and "is".

blocks.text: ASL is its own language with its own grammar, not English on the hands. When we write signs down we use a [[gloss]]: English words in capitals that name each sign.
ASL verbs don't change [[tense]]. Instead a time sign opens the [[sentence]] and sets the time for everything after it.

blocks.english: I went to the store yesterday.

blocks.text: A very common pattern is [[topic-comment]]: name what you're talking about, then say something about it. The topic is marked with raised eyebrows, a [[non-manual marker|non-manual-marker]].
Here the [[object]] BOOK moved to the front as the topic.

items: There are no signs for the [[articles|article]] a, an and the.
"And" is often shown with a pause or body shift instead of a [[conjunction]] sign.

blocks.text: For a [[yes/no question|yes-no-question]], raise your eyebrows. For a [[wh-question]], lower and draw your eyebrows together, and put the question sign at the end.
[[Pronouns|pronoun]] are made by pointing, and [[adjectives|adjective]] can come before or after the [[noun]]. Many [[adverbs|adverb]] are shown by changing how the [[verb]] moves.
